title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: US markets are closed for the weekend after Friday's rally (S&P 500 +0.5% to 7,743.41, Nasdaq +0.5% to 27,068.72, Dow +0.9% to 51,828.62); no new session data since Friday's close.
Markets: Heading into the new week, the 10-year Treasury yield sits near 5.17%, gold is near $4,285/oz, and oil is holding recent losses on hopes for a phased Strait of Hormuz reopening.

Companies: Corporate news was quiet over the weekend; markets are still digesting Friday's Akamai-Anthropic $11B+ multiyear cloud deal and the chip/AI rally (Micron, ON Semiconductor, PHLX Semi index) it helped fuel.

Macro/Policy: A stopgap funding bill signed in early September keeps the government funded through Dec. 11, taking a shutdown off the table ahead of the midterms, though the underlying fiscal fight remains unresolved.
Macro/Policy: Fed's Williams, Goolsbee and Logan made public appearances over the weekend with no fresh policy signals; futures still price elevated odds of another rate move in October.
Macro/Policy: Heavy data week ahead - JOLTS (Tue), the Fed's preferred PCE inflation gauge (Wed), ISM manufacturing (Thu), and the September jobs report (Fri Oct 2, ~90-100k jobs expected).
